# Chart management (his-backend `chartmanagement` + his-frontend `/chart-management`)

**Goal:** an Administrator can build SQL-driven charts from verified-safe, aggregate-only queries and publish them on
dashboards for access-group viewers, while the system keeps patient-identifying data out of every response.

**Docs:** module features: [module catalogue](../../modules/README.md) (linked on every story).

Plan and contract: `his-v3-ai/services-impl/202611/chart-management/` (`STEP-5-E2E-AUTOMATION.md`, `API-CONTRACT.md`,
`SECURITY-DESIGN.md`). Epic code `CHMGMT`.

Surfaces under test:

| Surface                                                                 | Target       | Spec folder                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| GraphQL `chartmanagement` module (12 queries + 11 mutations, 23 in all) | his-backend  | `tests/api/graphql/his-backend/chartmanagement/` |
| `/chart-management/*`: list, chart builder, layout builder, viewer      | his-frontend | `tests/web/his-frontend/chart-management/`       |

## User stories

- **US-CHMGMT-01** ([A11.04](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a11-04)) — As an Administrator I want to build a SQL-driven chart with verified safe SQL so that I can track operational metrics without exposing patient-identifying data.
- **US-CHMGMT-02** ([A11.04](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a11-04)) — As an Administrator I want to assemble charts into a dashboard with viewer-group access control so that only authorized groups see sensitive metrics.
- **US-CHMGMT-03** ([A11.04](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a11-04)) — As a viewer I want to open a dashboard and see rendered charts so that I can read aggregate operational data without risk of PHI exposure.
- **US-CHMGMT-04** ([A11.04](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a11-04)) — As a system I want to block suspicious SQL, enforce chunk-transport integrity, and suppress small cells automatically so that PHI is protected even when a chart author makes a mistake.
- **US-CHMGMT-05** ([A11.04](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a11-04)) — As an Administrator I want to export charts and dashboards to a JSON bundle file so that I can transfer them to another environment.
- **US-CHMGMT-06** ([A11.04](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a11-04)) — As an Administrator I want to import a bundle with a preview plan so that I can re-use existing charts and create missing ones safely.

## Status of this catalog

Verified 2026-11-08 on `TEST_ENV=local` (his-backend + his-frontend built locally, isolated local Redis, staging DB, three QA accounts), re-run after the
security-hardening merge of PR #4793: a row is `automated` only after it passed three runs in a row on the final code. API: three sequential full runs
of the 98 non-destructive cases (workers=1, local Redis flushed between runs: the decrypt lockout is per user, so `crypto.spec` cannot use
`--repeat-each`); the six `@destructive` cases (rate limit, kill switch, decrypt lockout) three times alone against the local Redis; web:
`--repeat-each=3`, chromium, workers=2. All green, no skips. Roles come from `env/.env.local` (git-ignored): author = `HIS_AUTH_*`, author2 =
`CHARTMGMT_AUTHOR2_*`, viewer = `CHARTMGMT_VIEWER_*` + `CHARTMGMT_VIEWER_ACG_ID`. TC-CHMGMT-150..169 pin the security-review findings
(C1, C2, H1, H3, H4, M5, M7); `viewer-role-matrix` (120..129) and TC-CHMGMT-031 cover "a viewer with the page ACL stays FORBIDDEN / NOT_FOUND".

TC-CHMGMT-170..195 cover HISv3-FEATURE-00242 (import/export bundle): added 2026-11-12. TC-CHMGMT-170 is a pure hash-algorithm unit test (no staging required).
TC-CHMGMT-171..188 are API-level and require both `author` and `author2` roles. TC-CHMGMT-189..194 are web-level and require a deployed his-frontend with the
import/export feature. TC-CHMGMT-191 and TC-CHMGMT-195 are `test.fixme` pending his-frontend #7546 + #7548: both verified green locally on branch
`tmp/verify-import-e2e`; fixme lifted once those FE PRs merge to staging.

Rows that stay `blocked` / `manual-only` / deferred keep their `Reason`. A web run against a cold Vite dev server needs
`EXPECT_TIMEOUT_MS=60000` (each page compiles on first load); `rate-limit.spec`, `kill-switch.spec` and `security-lockout.spec` must run alone on a local backend
with a local Redis (flush it between runs; a lockout cannot be lifted through the API) (the kill switch is a global Redis key).

## Running these specs

Roles (environment only, see `env/*.example`): `author` = `HIS_AUTH_*` (Administrator; SuperAdmin for the kill-switch
rows), `author2` = `CHARTMGMT_AUTHOR2_*` (four-eyes validator, cross-user token owner), `viewer` =
`CHARTMGMT_VIEWER_*` plus `CHARTMGMT_VIEWER_ACG_ID`. A spec whose role is not configured skips with the missing key names.

- **Test key.** Encrypted verifies use only `vectors/chart-sql-test-key.pub.pem`. The backend under test must be
  started with the private half of that TEST-ONLY key and the frontend with the public half as `VITE_APP_PUBLIC_KEY`;
  otherwise `ensureTestKey` skips the spec (see `vectors/README.md`).
- **Rate limits are per user.** Verify is 10/min/user, so `chartKit.verify` waits out a window (polling, no sleep) —
  a full API run takes several minutes. Five payload-decrypt failures in 15 min lock a user for 15 min: run
  `crypto.spec.ts` once per 15 min, never with `--repeat-each`.
- **Global-state cases** (`@destructive`): `rate-limit.spec.ts` (TC-CHMGMT-070) and `kill-switch.spec.ts`
  (TC-CHMGMT-080/081/082/095, also needs `CHARTMGMT_KILLSWITCH_OVERRIDE=true`) must run alone with `--workers=1`
  on a local backend; they never run on shared staging.
- **Audit rows** are read through the his-v3-ai DB harness (`db.py`, SELECT only, keyed on captured IDs / the SQL hash).
- **Web** runs chromium only, `--workers=2` in CI (4 vCPU / 3 GB).

```bash
npx playwright test tests/api/graphql/his-backend/chartmanagement/ --project=api-graphql
npx playwright test tests/web/his-frontend/chart-management/ --project="web-his-frontend-chromium" --workers=2
```

## Data lifecycle

Every chart title, purpose, dashboard name and slug carries `QA-E2E-<run> w<worker>`. Teardown is keyed on the literal
`chartID` / `chartDashboardID` returned by the create call (dashboards are deleted before charts, so `CHART_IN_USE`
cannot block). The first use of `chartKit` in a worker sweeps that worker slot's leftovers: it finds them by the
marker and then deletes each by the literal ID it received — never by count, position or time window.

## Frontend locator contract (provisional)

The his-frontend pages did not exist when the page objects were written. They assume these `data-testid`s (and the
Bahasa labels of `LAYOUT-DESIGN.md`); the frontend should add them, or the page objects change in one place
(`src/web/his-frontend/pages/chart-management/`).

| Page           | Test ids                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List           | `chart-mgmt-list`, `chart-mgmt-tab-dashboards`, `chart-mgmt-tab-charts`, `chart-mgmt-keyword`, `chart-mgmt-empty-state`                                                                                                                                       |
| Chart builder  | `chart-sql-editor`, `chart-patient-count-field`, `chart-verify-panel` (`data-status` = safe/warn/unsafe), `chart-violation-chip`, `chart-warning-chip`, `chart-token-countdown`, `chart-token-expired`, `chart-title-input`, `chart-purpose-input`            |
| Layout builder | `dashboard-builder`, `dashboard-name-input`, `dashboard-slug-input`, `dashboard-slug-error`, `dashboard-viewer-groups`, `dashboard-save-button`, `dashboard-row-preset-<ONE\|TWO\|TWO_LEFT\|TWO_RIGHT\|THREE>`, `dashboard-row-<n>`, `dashboard-cell-<n>-<m>` |
| Viewer         | `dashboard-view`, `dashboard-cell` (`data-chart-id`, `data-cell-state`), `chart-canvas`, `chart-cell-overlay`, `chart-suppression-notice`; denied/disabled slugs redirect to `/404`                                                                           |
